title: Crucible.app Live Fleet Observability Decision Trace

events.summary: Replace the ambiguous CodexBar directional-reference language with a selective adopt, adapt, and reject policy for the Crucible.app foundation.

decision.rationale: Calling CodexBar merely directional preserved the no-copy boundary but lost the useful judgment. Crucible.app should reuse field-tested menu bar lifecycle, state, refresh, and testing lessons while adapting the entire data boundary to one Crucible CLI client and refusing CodexBar-specific provider, probe, helper, widget, and release complexity.

result.learning: A reference project is safest when its transferable lessons and non-transferable product complexity are both explicit; otherwise directional guidance either becomes decorative or quietly turns into architecture parity.
